subject: Request: ad-hoc forensic panel for interleaved route spikes
messages:
From: Mina Haddad <mina_haddad@redwood.com>
To: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>, Jasmine Liu <jasmine_liu@redwood.com>
Cc: Samir Rao <samir.rao@acme.io>, Lauren <lauren@acme.io>
Date: Thu, 12 Jan 2028 09:15:00 -0800
Subject: Request: ad-hoc forensic panel for interleaved route spikes

Team —

We had a support alert from Acme this morning: repeated, interleaved spikes across several tenant routes with correlated token-cost upticks and tail-latency bursts. See attached screenshot (spike-screenshot.png). Acme is asking for a quick interactive panel they can use while debugging session-level behavior.

Ask: can we put together a short-term "forensic panel" in Console that combines the following, with linked drill-ins to traces/query results:
- per-route cost waterfall (breakdown by model variant + quantization profile)
- tail latency distribution (95/99/99.9) by tenant slice
- active KV-cache hit rate and inferred prefix reuse for the timeframe
- sample chat traces (link to trace playback) and the top N callchains causing token blowouts

Constraints: timeline is tight — Acme wants an interim view by EOD Monday for their on-call. Long-term we should fold this into the route inspector, but for now something ad-hoc is fine.

I attached a simple SQL I ran to get the first-pass correlation (ad-hoc-sql.txt). Marcus / Kim — can you advise whether the cost-waterfall can be surfaced as an embeddable widget (interactive breakdown) and what telemetry we should sample? Jasmine — can you run a quick tenant-level pivot for Acme (tenant id acme-corp-prod) and attach any immediate findings?

Thanks —
Mina
Mina Haddad
Product Manager, Observability
Redwood Inference

From: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>
To: Mina Haddad <mina_haddad@redwood.com>, Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>, Jasmine Liu <jasmine_liu@redwood.com>
Cc: Samir Rao <samir.rao@acme.io>
Date: Thu, 12 Jan 2028 11:02:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Request: ad-hoc forensic panel for interleaved route spikes

+1 on the ad-hoc panel. A few quick notes from infra:
- We can produce a cost waterfall if we have per-token attribution (model variant, quantized vs fp16, and service tier). The query is reasonably cheap but we need to bound the time window — long tails mean a lot of rows.
- KV-cache metrics: we currently emit cache_hit_ratio per runtime host; stitching that per-tenant requires the tenant->host mapping (I can do that if you want).
- For tail latency, we should sample full callchains at 1% but increase to 5% for suspect tenants (like acme-corp-prod) while we triage.

Possible pitfalls: batching behaviors can make token-cost look worse than latency; we should surface average batch size and burst buckets in the panel.

I can spin up the embeddable waterfall widget prototype on a temporary route (obs/forensic-panel/<id>) by EOD Monday if we scope it to the last 24h. If Mina wants a wider window, schedule slips to Tuesday.

—Marcus
Marcus Lin
SRE Lead, Serving Runtime
Redwood Inference

Mina / Marcus —

This makes sense. A couple clarifying questions to scope the panel:
1) Time window: do we want last 24h (fast) or rolling 7d (more context)? For EOD Monday, 24h is safest.
2) Output level: do we show per-request cost breakdown or aggregated per-session? Per-request is more precise but noisy.
3) Access controls: Acme should only see their tenant slices; we need to ensure the panel enforces tenant-level filters.

If we do 24h, I can attach a heatmap snippet and a quick SQL that aggregates the token-cost by model variant and tenant; I'll drop it into the Drive folder and link to OBS-842 (our Jira).

Also: Marcus — the embeddable widget should accept a sample_rate override so we can bump sampling without redeploying. That will make triage much faster.

Thanks,
Kimberly

Date: Sat, 14 Jan 2028 14:28:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Request: ad-hoc forensic panel for interleaved route spikes

Mina / all —

I ran a quick pivot over the last 24h for tenant acme-corp-prod. Key findings attached (acme-query-results.csv):
- There are repeated small bursts from a handful of session ids that show average batch size > 8 and correspond to a specific model variant (redwood-v2-8q8). That variant has higher per-token cost when quantized due to kernel fallbacks on a few hosts.
- KV-cache hit rate for the tenant is ~42% during normal times, dropping to ~18% during spikes — likely a session-level cold-start pattern.
- Top 3 callchains by token spend are: model decode -> post-processing rerank -> tool integration. I included sample trace ids.

Recommendation for the panel: show a small table of suspect session ids with links to trace playback, a toggle to increase sample_rate to 5% for just those sessions, and the cost waterfall by variant with a selectable bucket (per-request / per-session).

I'll keep digging; if you want I can produce a condensed CSV for sharing with Acme (redacted) by Monday morning.

—Jasmine
Jasmine Liu
Data Analyst, Observability
Redwood Inference

Thanks everyone — great thread. Quick summary / next steps: 
- Scope: 24h rolling window for the interim panel; tenant-filtered for Acme only. (Kim will drop the heatmap SQL in Drive.)
- Deliverable: prototype embeddable waterfall + tail-latency distribution + suspect-session table with sample-rate toggle. Marcus to stand up the temporary obs/forensic-panel prototype (EOD Monday).
- Data: Jasmine to produce the redacted CSV for Acme and a short list of callchains/trace ids.
- Access: Product will ensure tenant access restriction; Security to sign off if we expose traces externally.

Samir / Lauren — we will share the redacted view Monday morning and schedule a 30m walkthrough after that. Apologies for the scramble — we'll aim for a stable route inspector integration in the Q1 roadmap.

Action items (owners):
- Marcus: prototype waterfall widget + sampling override on obs/forensic-panel (owner: marcus_lin).
- Kimberly: heatmap SQL + Drive link (owner: kimberly_park).
- Jasmine: redacted CSV and trace list (owner: jasmine_liu).
- Mina: stakeholder sync & confirm Security review (owner: mina_haddad).
